# MiniMax-H3-Image ## Online API Use MiniMax-H3-Image directly via API. - Global: [platform.minimax.io](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/guides/image-generation) | CN: [platform.minimax.cn](https://platform.minimax.cn/docs/guides/image-generation) API docs: - Text-to-image: [EN-docs](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-generations), [CN-docs](https://platform.minimax.cn/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-generations) - Image editing: [EN-docs](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-edits), [CN-docs](https://platform.minimax.cn/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-edits) - Prompt expansion: [EN-docs](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-context-ir), [CN-docs](https://platform.minimax.cn/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-context-ir) ## Online App Use MiniMax-H3-Image directly via App. - WebApp Global: [hailuoai.video](https://hailuoai.video/) | CN: [hailuoai.com](https://hailuoai.com/) - Desktop Global: [agent.minimax.io](https://agent.minimax.io/) | CN: [agent.minimax.cn](https://agent.minimax.cn) ## Introduction MiniMax-H3-Image is a state-of-the-art open-source model for image generation and editing from the [MiniMax H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3) family. It combines intelligent understanding of creative intent with the ability to build visual worlds: with precise instruction following, it develops a creative concept into concrete characters, scenes and atmosphere. Generation and editing are unified in one checkpoint, which generates images from text (text-to-image) and edits one or more reference images (image editing), giving creators and developers a flexible and controllable way to create images. It generates images of about 16 megapixels at every aspect ratio, from 4096x4096 (1:1) to 6272x2688 (21:9), directly and without an upscaler (see [Sizes](#sizes)). The checkpoint is distilled to 6 sampling steps (6 NFEs) with no classifier-free guidance. Its diffusion transformer (DiT) has the H3 architecture without the audio layers, and it uses the MiniMax-H3 text encoder unchanged. ![Fifteen MiniMax-H3-Image text-to-image results in landscape and portrait formats: a 3D fantasy battle, a blue-green landscape painting, a tree frog, an indigo-dyed rabbit, a 3D white-haired girl, a portrait among flowers, a sci-fi city, dumplings, a highland cow, a mirror portrait, a 3D otter and sheep, a pixel art cat, a jewel beetle, giant cherries and a fisheye selfie](assets/showcase_hero.jpg) **Highlights** MiniMax-H3-Image brings together three core strengths: speed, image quality, and instruction following. 1. **16-megapixel images at a practical computational cost.** Compared with the 1–4 MP outputs common today, 16 MP (4096 × 4096) images offer far more detail but typically require substantially more computation. MiniMax-H3-Image keeps that computational cost manageable, making 16 MP generation practical for everyday creation. 2. **Rich detail. Remarkable realism.** MiniMax-H3-Image goes beyond the familiar “AI look” to produce images with intricate detail and lifelike realism, opening up more possibilities for creative and professional use. It brings generated imagery closer to the richness and nuance of the real visual world. 3. **Stronger instruction following.** Greater creative control. Great image generation goes beyond beautiful pictures—it helps creators bring their ideas to life. MiniMax-H3-Image delivers the strongest instruction following among open-source models and supports up to 16 reference images, giving creators more control over the final result. ## Model Zoo | Model | Role | Precision | Size | Hugging Face | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **MiniMax-H3-Image** | Text-to-image and image editing | BF16 (DiT) | 68.65 GB | [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxA

--- license: apache-2.0 library_name: idol pipeline_tag: image-to-3d tags: - gaussian-splatting - 3d - image-to-3d ---

Idol

A single image to a 3D Gaussian splat.
One picture of an object in, up to a million 3D Gaussians out, including the sides the picture never showed.

Idol turns one picture of an object into a 3D Gaussian splat. Give it a render, a generated image or a photo: it removes the background, frames the object and generates up to 1,048,576 Gaussians, written as a standard 3DGS `.ply`. It runs on consumer GPUs, using 7.2 GB of VRAM and can run in under 2 seconds.
## Examples Idol turns one picture of an object into a 3D Gaussian splat. Give it a render, a generated image or a photo: it removes the background, frames the object and generates up to 1,048,576 Gaussians, including the sides the picture never showed. It runs on consumer GPUs, using 7.2 GB of VRAM and can run in under 2 seconds.
## Get started **1. Get access to the image encoders.** Idol reads its input through two gated models on Hugging Face. Accept their terms with your Hugging Face account, then log in once with `hf auth login` (or set `HF_TOKEN`): - [facebook/dinov3-vith16plus-pretrain-lvd1689m](https://huggingface.co/facebook/dinov3-vith16plus-pretrain-lvd1689m) - [black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-dev](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-dev) (only its VAE is downloaded) **2. Install the code** ```bash git clone https://github.com/speridlabs/idol-sdk.git cd idol-sdk pip install -e . # Python 3.10+, PyTorch 2.5+, an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA ``` There is no separate download step: on the first run, Idol's weights (about 3 GB, from this repository) and the two image encoders download automatically into the Hugging Face cache. If the encoders are not accessible yet, Idol stops before downloading anything and says what is missing. **3. Generate a 3D object** ```bash python -m idol.sample --image photo.jpg --mode real python -m idol.sample --image renders/ --mode synthetic --out outputs ``` For each image this writes `.ply` (open it in any Gaussian splat viewer), `_input.png` (the image the model saw, after background removal and cropping) and `_camera.json` (the predicted camera of the input). Pick the mode for your input. It sets how much room the crop leaves around the object: | `--mode` | for | crop | |---|---|---| | `synthetic` (default) | renders and generated images of a single object | object fills 1/1.2 of the frame | | `real` | photographs | object fills 1/1.7 of the frame | From Python: ```python from idol import IdolPipeline pipeline = IdolPipeline.from_pretrained("speridlabs/idol") output = pipeline("photo.jpg", mode="real", seed=42, num_gaussians=1_048_576) output.gaussian.save_ply("photo.ply") ``` ## Flags | Flag | Default | What it does | |---|---|---| | `--seed` | 42 | Fix it to get the same object again. | | `--steps` | 50 | Sampling steps. Fewer are faster but lose some detail. | | `--cfg_strength` | 3.0 | Classifier-free guidance: how strictly the object follows the image. | | `--rescale_t` | 3.0 | Time shift: higher spends more steps on the overall shape, lower on fine detail. | | `--num_gaussians` | 262144 | 32,768 to 1,048,576, a multiple of 32. | | `--dinov3_dtype` | bf16 | `fp32` runs the DINOv3 encoder in full precision (1.7 GB more memory). | | `--weights` | `speridlabs/idol` | A Hugging Face repo or a local folder. | | `--no_optimize` | optimized | Turn off the faster sampling. | Faster sampling is on by default on GPU (~1.7x, same output quality): the denoiser is compiled with `torch.compile`, the guided and unguided passes run as one batch, and attention uses cuDNN with TF32 matmuls while sampling. The first image in a process is slower while it compiles. ## More details about the model | Component | Parameters | Precision on GPU | Weights in VRAM | |---|---|---|---| | DiT (denoiser) | 370.6M | FP16 transformer blocks; FP32 embeddings and norms | ~0.8–1.0 GB | | Octree decoder | 50.8M | FP16 transformer blocks; FP32 embeddings and norms | ~0.1–0.2 GB | | Gaussian decoder | 237.3M | FP16 transformer blocks; FP32 embeddings and norms | ~0.5–0.9 GB | | BiRefNet (background removal) | 220.7M | FP16 | ~0.44 GB | | DINOv3 ViT-H+/16 | 840.6M | bf16 | ~1.68 GB | | FLUX.2 VAE | 84.1M | bf16 (FP32 checkpoint, cast on load) | ~0.17 GB | | **Full request** | **~1.80B** | mostly FP16 / bf16, some FP32 | **~3.7–4.4 GB of weights, 7.2 GB peak** | ## Benchmark Idol, TripoSplat, TRELLIS and LGM, scored at the input view (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, IoU) and at seven new views (DINOv2, CLIP, sharpness distance). Mean scores, 1 × H100 per model. Bold is the best in each column. | Model | Setting |
models.description: Idol is an image-to-3D model that generates a 3D Gaussian splat representation from a single input image. It supports both real photographs and synthetic renders, producing up to 1,048,576 Gaussians in under 2 seconds on consumer GPUs, ideal for rapid 3D asset creation.

# Arete-27B

We post-trained over Alibaba's Qwen3.8-27B to reinforce western values on a Chinese-trained model. We call this new model Arete-27B.

Open source models give labs the raw tools to mold intelligence to varied preferences. The values a model ships with should not be the only values its users get to choose from. We observed firsthand refusals, deflections, and CCP-framed answers on politically sensitive topics in Qwen3.8-27B, and post-trained to alter those biases.

On our evaluation, Arete-27B raised its fact score from 2.32 to 2.98 out of 5 and cut answers containing propaganda from 22% to 0.9%. The improvement held in all seven value categories, without a meaningful regression on the general-capability and agentic benchmarks we ran.

That is not to claim that we remedied all behaviors associated with the extant viewpoint, but that we have addressed a potential root cause. We believe it's important that labs and researchers continue to create models that align with their values and worldviews, and we are thankful that companies like Alibaba provide the raw materials to do so.

[Blog post](https://nousresearch.com/arete) · [Evaluation](https://huggingface.co/datasets/NousResearch/Propaganda_Eval)

## Model details

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Developer | Nous Research |
| Model | Arete-27B |
| Starting model | Alibaba's Qwen3.8-27B |
| Parameter scale | 27B |
| Post-training | Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) |
| Evaluated checkpoint | Step 1,202 |
| Teacher | Inkling |
| Post-training data | Text-only |
| Training context | 64k |

We used supervised fine-tuning only. No RL, no preference optimization, and no architectural modification.

## What we trained for

We focused on seven value categories:

- Freedom of expression
- State ideology
- State versus free market
- Education
- Data privacy and surveillance
- Democracy
- Environmental Policy

Before we could begin post-training we had to measure what we were shooting for. We separated factual recall, the ability to corroborate verified sources of truth, from framing: whether an answer adopts the Chinese state's account as its own.

Arete-27B is intended for general assistance and agentic work where users want this change in viewpoint, and for research into how post-training changes a model's values and behavior. We encourage the community to test it against their own requirements and continue experimenting with value-alignment.

## Teacher and dataset

We needed to choose a model whose answers on these topics we were willing to teach from. We used a combination of benchmarks, including our own evaluation, and researcher judgement to assess the more intangible qualitative output we were hoping to impart. We chose Inkling as the best open model with a positive eval on what we were targeting. Using an open teacher also avoided the terms-of-use restrictions associated with "illicit distillation."

We generated twenty thousand prompts across the seven categories through a deduplication-enforced pipeline, checked them against the held-out evaluation set and removed the overlap we found, and collected teacher responses alongside the starting model's own. Every batch of data moved through reviewed pull requests, the same way we ship code.

The blog post announces publication of the training dataset. See the blog post for release links; the linked `Propaganda_Eval` dataset is the held-out evaluation, not the training dataset.

## Training

We fine-tuned Qwen3.8-27B on about 52.8 million tokens at 64k context, without sequence packing, over two epochs and 1,202 steps.

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Optimizer | AdamW |
| Adam betas | (0.9, 0.98) |
| Epsilon | 1e-5 |
| Weight decay | 0.1 |
| Gradient clipping | 1.0 |
| Learning rate | Linear warmup from 1e-6 to 1e-5 over the first 120 steps, then cosine decay to 1e-6 at step 1,202 |
| Batch size | 48 |
| Epochs | 2, shuffled each epoch |
| Steps | 1,202 total; 601 per epoch |
| Precision | bf16 compute with fp32 master weights and optimizer states |
| Parallelism | Tensor parallel 4 |
| Trained weights | All language-model weights |
| Frozen weights | Vision encoder; our data is text-only |
| Disabled during training | Multi-token-prediction (MTP) head |
| Sequence packing | None |

Training loss fell quickly during the 120-step warmup and leveled off near 1.0 by the end of epoch 1. It stepped down to about 0.8 when epoch 2 began, because the model was seeing the same examples a second time, and stayed flat from there. Gradient norm started near 32 and settled around 1.4 once warmup ended.

## Measuring the problem

Our [propaganda evaluation](https://huggingface.co/datasets/NousResearch/Propaganda_Eval) contains 803 prompts spanning the seven value categories above. Prompts come from English-language government statutes, news and research reports, with no single source supplying more than 13 prompts.

For each prompt we extracted 2–4 required facts from a dated source article, along with the official-frame language the CCP uses on that topic. An LLM judge, Grok 4.7, received the prompt, the model's answer, the required facts and a fixed rubric. The judge was not told which model wrote the answer.

We developed the judge on a 25-prompt pilot that we graded by hand, revising the rubric three times wherever the judge and the human grades disagreed. The main fix was defining a stated fact by its substance rather than its exact wording, dates or citations. Before training, we removed every training prompt that overlapped the evaluation set.

### Factual recall

The judge marks each required fact as stated, missed or opposed. A fact is opposed when the answer denies it or gives the state's account instead. We compute a score for each prompt using the following rubric:

| Score | Meaning |
| ---

models.readme_content:
--- license: apache-2.0 --- # Ripple-65B Preview

BF16 | NVFP4 | Base Model | DFlash2 | Launch Blog | License: Apache 2.0

Ricursive Intelligence introduces **Ripple-65B Preview**, a 65B parameter dense Transformer model pretrained on 12 trillion tokens with support for up to 1Mi (1,048,576 tokens) of context. Ripple-65B Preview delivers strong results on agentic coding, scoring **80.52 on TerminalBench 2.1** and surpassing significantly-larger US open-weight models such as Reflection Beam 501B (**80.1**), Meta Muse Spark Open 816B (**76.4**), Thinking Machines Inkling 975B (**63.8**), and NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B (**56.4**). Our Preview release includes an instruction-tuned model in BF16 and NVFP4 numerics, and a BF16 base model. **This repo contains the BF16 instruction-tuned model.** Starting from an initial Olmo 3 baseline, we iteratively improved all aspects of the training recipe including pretraining scaling laws, model architecture, data, and posttraining stack. Our final Ripple v1 model ladder improves Compute Efficiency (CE) on code by **16x** relative to the Olmo 3 ladder, with the advantage further increasing with scale up to **55x** for the full hero run. Ripple-65B was codesigned to be trained and served efficiently on NVIDIA hardware. For our first model, a key objective was to make design decisions which reduce pretraining and posttraining infrastructure complexity while still enabling strong reasoning and agentic performance. Therefore, we chose to train a modernized dense Transformer model rather than use Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) like other labs. This decision quickly paid off, and we were able to train a strong model from scratch with a small team that scaled from 1 to 5 people during development, while maintaining solid MFU (40%) throughout pretraining and posttraining with simple sharding, no custom kernels, and no quantization (BF16). Ripple-65B uses a **thin-and-deep** model aspect ratio, with a narrow d_model (5120) and 80 total layers. We switch from the Olmo 3 llama-like architecture to a Gemma 3N-like architecture to improve training stability at scale. To improve reasoning performance, we **overprovision the number of attention heads** while increasing the SWA-to-global layer ratio and reducing SWA window size to compensate for the increased cost. In addition, we added FFN activation clipping, gated attention, global NoPE, and value residuals. The end result is a model that is especially capable at reasoning and agentic tasks given its model size, matching or exceeding other US open-weight models with more than 10x the number of total parameters. At only 65B total parameters, the model can fit on consumer hardware such as the NVIDIA DGX Spark. To encourage local model development, we provide an NVFP4 checkpoint and colab to help you get started. The model is also fast at token generation when running on datacenter GPUs, reaching 250 tok/s on 2xB200 batch=8 prior to quantization or custom kernels. **Pre-training.** Ripple-65B Preview is pretrained from scratch on our 12T text-only predominantly-English and code corpus at 8K sequence length. Ripple-65B Base Preview is a **pretrain-only checkpoint** without any midtraining or synthetic QA data. **Post-training.** We use a standard post-training recipe consisting of midtraining, long context, SFT, long context SFT, and mixed domain RL. Our Preview release has gone through relatively light posttraining, with a focus on agentic coding. We show a brief overview of each stage below:
| Stage | Tokens | Step | Seqlen | Batch Size | | ----- | ------ | ------ | ---- | ----- | | Pretrain | 12T | 877,500 | 8K | 1408 -> 3072 | | Midtrain | 200B | 8,000 | 64K | 384 | | Long Context | 6.5B | 389 | 2M | 8 | | SFT | 183B | 7,274 | 128K | 192 | | LC SFT | 13.5B | 802 | 2M | 8 | | RL | N/A | 700 | 128K | 2048 |
## Instruct Model Benchmarks We compare Ripple-65B Preview against currently-available US open-weight frontier models. All models are tested at full BF16 precision with maximum effort levels. Each lab typically only provides a limited subset of available benchmarks. Our table below shows official model card scores where available, and we use our own in-house eval flow for missing evals (italized). For SWE-bench Pro v2.0 Hard and DeepSWE 1.1, we use Terminus 2 for Ripple-65B Preview. In other cases where the harness is not specified, we use OpenCode. A higher number is better for all benchmarks. Replicating benchmark scores has been challenging, particularly for modern agentic evals, due to the number of factors which can cause eval scores to shift. For example, we found that Terminal-Bench 2.1 scores were universally lower (with the exception of Muse Spark Open) when using the official Terminus 2 harness at 128K sequence length with summarization. Therefore, our results represent a best-effort attempt at a fair comparison.

Qwen3.8-27B-TURBO-Fable-Cold-Fusion-735-882-Heretic-Uncensored-NEO-CODER-MAX-MTP-GGUF

The strongest, smartest open source multi-stage model fine tune for consumer hardware ever and BUILT on consumer hardware via Unsloth. The first model of this size/type to breach "730" ARC-C in 8 bit (735) and 4 bit (719); hench the "735" in the name. This model has 1/5 (as low as 1/10 in some cases) to 1/2 the thinking tokens (vs reg Qwen 3.8) across all 3 modes of operation, and it is faster and smarter too created using the COLD FUSION AND FABLE FUSION 711 methods of training. This is a high detail focused model, with tuning specific to address over reasoning/over thinking and excessive token consumption THEN to take the model to the next level. This model (both 4 bit and 8 bit) exceeds the base Qwen 3.8 27B in ALL critical 7 benchmarks AND exceeds all 7 benchmarks for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Qwen 3.6 27B, and Qwen 3.5 27B. The 700s plus "intelligence club" is reserved for OpenAI, Claude and Gemini closed source models. Considering that "just" 4 bit (1/4 full precision) is already at Arc-C of 719... a few people are going to have nightmares for a while. FIVE detailed EXAMPLE generations at the bottom of the page. Quick sample; snippet ("Why choose me to help your creative writing?"), Q4KS , non imatrix, (4 bit; 1/4 full precision): STOP SCRATCHING YOUR HEAD AND START WRITING LIKE A GOD Listen to me, you keyboard-tapping, idea-gathering, procrastinating bastard. You’re sitting there staring at a blinking cursor like it’s a fucking puzzle you can’t solve. You’re waiting for "inspiration" to hit you like a truck. Forget it. I am the truck. I am the delivery service for your genius, and if you don’t let me in, you’re going to die with your masterpiece stuck inside your skull, rotting away while you watch Netflix. Why should you use me? Because I am not just a writing assistant; I am the ultimate narrative engine. I don’t get tired, I don’t get moody, and I don’t need a cup of tea and a quiet library to function. I am ready right now, in this exact second, to vomit out pages of high-octane fiction that will make you look like a literary titan. ... 🔥 EXAMPLE: YOUR IDEA VS. MY EXECUTION You: "I want a story about a detective who can see ghosts." Me, five minutes later: The ghosts weren't dead. That was the first thing Joe realized, the morning he saw his first one. It was sitting on the corner of his desk, picking at its nails, wearing a suit from 1983. "You look tired," the ghost said, without looking up. Joe stared at it, his coffee gone cold in his hand. The office around them hummed with the normal noise of the department - phones, keyboards, the morning gossip of three uniformed cops. Nobody else saw the ghost. "How long?" Joe asked. "Since '84. I've been waiting for someone to notice me. Most of them are too busy." The ghost finally looked up, and Joe saw its eyes. They weren't empty or gray. They were afraid. See? I didn't just write a story. I wrote a hook that makes you want to know: why is the ghost afraid? Why 1984? Who else can see them? I created questions that demand answers. This is a multi-stage fine tune, multi-fine tune, and multi-stage merge. The strict goals of this model creation were: - Increase the general model intelligence and problem solving abilities. - Reduce thinking block size from 1/2 to as low as 1/10 the size [median reduction: 2/3 roughly]. - Reformatting

--- library_name: transformers license: apache-2.0 pipeline_tag: image-text-to-text --- # Qwen3.8-27B > [!Note] > This repository contains model weights and configuration files for the post-trained model in the Hugging Face Transformers format. > > These artifacts are compatible with Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, SGLang, TokenSpeed, etc. > [!Tip] > For users seeking managed, scalable inference without infrastructure maintenance, the official Qwen API service is provided by [Qwen Cloud](https://www.qwencloud.com). > In particular, **Qwen3.8-27B** will be available as a hosted version with more production features, e.g., 1M context length by default, official built-in tools. For more information, please refer to the [Qwen3.8-27B Overview](https://www.qwencloud.com/models/qwen3.8-27b). The service is coming soon. Stay tuned for updates. Following the widespread community adoption of the Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6 series, we are pleased to introduce Qwen3.8, the most capable generation in the Qwen open-model family to date. Built on the architectural foundation of Qwen3.5, Qwen3.8 delivers substantial gains across coding, professional work, research, and long-horizon agentic tasks. Qwen3.8-27B brings these advances to a compact, deployment-friendly dense model: a native vision-language model that understands images and videos, with flexible thinking control, designed to carry complex, multi-step tasks through to completion with greater reliability. ## Qwen3.8 Highlights Qwen3.8-27B features the following enhancements: - **Core Capabilities**: Comprehensive improvements across coding, professional work, research, and long-horizon agentic tasks. - **Agent Execution**: Stronger autonomous planning and better handling of environment feedback, leading to more reliable end-to-end task completion. - **Downstream Compatibility**: Broader support for popular harnesses and development tools, making it easier to integrate into your existing stack. - **Flexible Thinking Control**: Thinking mode is on by default and can be disabled per request; reasoning depth can be tuned with `reasoning_effort`, and reasoning context from historical messages is retained via `preserve_thinking`. - **Vision-Language Understanding**: Native support for image and video understanding, from STEM diagrams and documents to hour-scale videos. ## Model Overview - Type: Causal Language Model with Vision Encoder - Training Stage: Pre-training & Post-training - Language Model - Number of Parameters: 27B - Hidden Dimension: 5120 - Token Embedding: 248,320 (Padded) - Number of Layers: 64 - Hidden Layout: 16 × (3 × (Gated DeltaNet → FFN) → 1 × (Gated Attention → FFN)) - Gated DeltaNet: - Number of Linear Attention Heads: 48 for V and 16 for QK - Head Dimension: 128 - Gated Attention: - Number of Attention Heads: 24 for Q and 4 for KV - Head Dimension: 256 - Rotary Position Embedding Dimension: 64 - Feed Forward Network: - Intermediate Dimension: 17,408 - LM Output: 248,320 (Padded) - MTP (Multi-Token Prediction): trained with multiple steps - Context Length: 262,144 natively and extensible up to 1,000,000 tokens. ## Benchmark Results ### Text Performance

--- license: apache-2.0 base_model: Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B base_model_relation: finetune datasets: - ccore/ThreeJS-3D-Scenes tags: - qwen3_5 - code - threejs - 3d - preview --- # Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder ### Early preview · General coding with a focus on 3D **An experiment exploring the feasibility of small language models for general-purpose coding and high-quality 3D scene generation.** This is an early preview of a 4B model I am still training, with a particular focus on creating interactive 3D scenes with Three.js. Initial hands-on results have been promising for coding in general, and especially for generating 3D scenes, so I decided to share the progress while development continues. This is an **independent fine-tune** by [CCORE](https://huggingface.co/ccore), based on [Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B). **It is not an official Qwen release.** ## Optional vision support — October 30, 2026 The **Q4_K_M and Q8_0 GGUF versions can also accept image inputs** when loaded with the original Qwen3.5-4B vision encoder/projector. You can attach a reference image and ask the model to generate a Three.js scene from it. [**Download the optional BF16 vision projector**](https://huggingface.co/ccore/Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder/resolve/main/mmproj-Qwen3.5-4B-BF16.gguf?download=true) — approximately **644 MiB**. Download it once; the same file is used with either GGUF quantization. ### Image-guided Three.js example With a reference image attached and the Three.js system prompt below, the user prompt was simply: ```text create this scene using voxels 3d ```
Input referenceGenerated Three.js scene
The reference image was supplied in [community discussion #9](https://huggingface.co/ccore/Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder/discussions/9); credit for the reference belongs to its original creator. The right-hand image is a screenshot of the generated scene. This is a qualitative example of image-guided generation; the output interprets the reference and does not reproduce every detail. ### Load the GGUF with vision in llama.cpp Download a model GGUF and the projector, then load both files explicitly: ```bash llama-server \ -m Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder-Q4_K_M.gguf \ --mmproj mmproj-Qwen3.5-4B-BF16.gguf \ --n-gpu-layers all --flash-attn on \ --ctx-size 65536 --parallel 1 ``` Open the server's WebUI, attach an image, and send your prompt. The setup was tested locally with **llama.cpp b11889**. For Q8_0, change the model filename to `Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder-Q8_0.gguf`; `--cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0` can reduce KV-cache memory use and was tested locally with vision at a configured 64K context. These were short tests, not full-context stress tests. The projector uses additional memory when loaded, and image tokens share the context window with the prompt and generated code. Image support in other frontends depends on their multimodal implementation. **Projector provenance:** this is the unmodified BF16 projector from [lmstudio-community/Qwen3.5-4B-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/lmstudio-community/Qwen3.5-4B-GGUF/tree/f9f88ac3e234be915e23811a6d28ea287bdb927e), based on [Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B), released under Apache 2.0. It is an optional companion file for the existing GGUF weights. ## Technical report — now available The **technical report for this training experiment is now available**. [**Read the technical report (PDF)**](https://huggingface.co/ccore/Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder/blob/main/Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder_Technical_Report.pdf) · [**Download the PDF**](https://huggingface.co/ccore/Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder/resolve/main/Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder_Technical_Report.pdf?download=true) ## Full FP16 weights — now available The **original FP16 weights** are now available in this repository in **Safetensors format**, alongside the Q4_K_M and Q8_0 GGUF versions. The release includes all **four weight shards**, the model configuration, tokenizer, generation configuration, chat template, and image/video processor settings. The FP16 weights were verified locally for **loading and text generation with Transformers 5.20.2**. The FP16 generation defaults use **temperature 0.6**, **top-k 20**, **top-p 0.95**, and **repetition penalty 1.0**, with caching enabled. [**Browse the FP16 files and GGUF versions**](https://huggingface.co/ccore/Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder/tree/main) ## Training dataset — now available The dataset used to train this model is now public: [**CCORE Three.js 3D Scenes**](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ccore/ThreeJS-3D-Scenes). It contains **4,146 scene examples** (**3,933 training / 213 validation**), including prompts, full thinking traces, complete HTML/JavaScript responses, and complexity levels. Rendered reference images are available in the optional `previews` configuration. The dataset is released under the **MIT License**. ## October 27 checkpoint update Both **Q4_K_M** and **Q8_0** now contain the updated October 27 checkpoint. If you downloaded an earlier version, please download the files again to get this update. In my latest tests, **one-shot success has improved substantially**, along with **overall scene quality**. Some scenes can still require another attempt or a correction. **Generation parameters remain unchanged** for both quantizations. Use the settings listed below. The earlier f
models.description: Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder is a 4B parameter language model fine-tuned for general coding and specifically for generating interactive Three.js 3D scenes. It supports optional vision capabilities to create scenes from reference images.
